correctness.rationale: The final theorem is restricted to the positive fixed-total-population simplex N=S+I+R=N0=b/d, k1=(d+gamma)/N0, k2=k1(1+gamma/(d+nu))/N0-epsilon/N0, 0<=epsilon<k1(1+gamma/(d+nu)), with all parameters positive and a single interior initial state fixed as epsilon->0. Direct independent symbolic expansion of the original ODE yields the exact system I′=-D_epsilon(I)-B_epsilon(I)w, w′=-(rho-aB_epsilon)w+aD_epsilon, w=R-aI, D=I^2(epsilon+C_epsilon I)/(1+alpha I^2), C_epsilon=C0-(1+a)epsilon/N0, B=I(k1+k2I)/(1+alpha I^2). At equilibrium w=0, D>0 for I>0 excludes all endemic equilibria; positively invariant compact simplex, planar index/Poincare-Bendixson and local one-sided attracting zero/negative center drift imply global convergence to disease-free point (boundary omega-limits force the same equilibrium). Independent differentiation confirms G′(z)=-1/[z^2(1+z)] and dG/dtau=-I′/[I^2(epsilon+C0 I)] for z=C0 I/epsilon, tau=epsilon^2t/C0. The stable fast w equation and Gronwall/variation of constants yield |w(t)| <= transient exponential + K(epsilon I^2+I^3), uniformly close to epsilon=0; this controls fixed-epsilon limits tI=1/epsilon and, at epsilon=0, tI^2=1/(2C0). Integrating G with a uniform entrance time T_delta for fixed interior initial data and a scaled transient error O(epsilon^2/I(T_delta)^2) proves locally uniform convergence to G^{-1}(tau) on compact subintervals tau>0. Independent exact sympy calculation confirms all key algebra, and a rational parameter integration gives supplementary numerical consistency only. Infinite-time and parameter-uniform results rely on analytic estimates, not verifier output or finite sampling.
residual_risks: Planar omega-limit proof presupposes standard Poincare-Bendixson/index exclusion and local center-manifold attraction; these textbook results were used under the compact positive simplex and strict interior assumption, not re-proved from first principles.

Endpoint scales are pointwise in epsilon for t->infinity; uniform crossover is proven only on compact positive tau intervals and fixed interior initial data, not at tau=0 or uniformly across arbitrary parameter-dependent tiny seeds.
Stochastic populations, zero-infection boundary data, negative epsilon and non-invariant initial totals fall outside the claim.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge qualified PASS for the combined, parameter-family, physical-time, globally seeded singular crossover, not for basic extinction, disease-free global stability, pitchfork bifurcation, or either elementary fixed-parameter center-decay mechanism. Original Zhang--Li 2023 model Eq.2, Theorem 3 and Theorem 4 were read in their full original 24-page CC BY manuscript and already give global extinction in the no-endemic regime and qualitative R0=1 pitchfork center degeneracy. The inspected source contains no locally-uniform epsilon->0 crossover with fixed positive initial data, physical-time C0/epsilon^2 normalization and infinite-scaled-amplitude entrance G^{-1}. The full nearby published 2026 mathematical findings concern distinct multiple-exposure S,I or predator-prey fields, not the exact SIRS family. A generic cubic-quadratic normal form suggests the limiting function, but converting it to the full global basin and nonuniform time scale needs the stated fast-variable estimates. The title/wording and lack of search hits are not novelty proofs, and an older implicit general singular-perturbation theorem is residual risk.
residual_risks: Basic algebraic t^-1 and t^-1/2 rates are standard local consequences of Zhang--Li 2023 qualitative center dynamics; novelty is assigned only to the combined uniformly scaled full-basin original-time crossover.

A general normal-form singular-perturbation theorem for cubic/quadratic flows may implicitly imply the G inverse profile without naming this SIRS model; no decisive explicit covering theorem was identified in actual searches.
Resultary similarity searching and the inspected primary literature are finite; historical priority in inaccessible or poorly indexed older critical-slowing literature is not certified.

value.rationale: The codimension-two meeting of R0=1 and the source pitchfork edge is a natural dynamical boundary in an established nonlinear SIRS epidemiological model. The result quantifies a previously qualitative transition with exact original-time extinction constants, a nontrivial epsilon^-2 crossover time scale, and an initial-data-independent inverse-log scaling profile for any fixed infected interior state; it remains useful for testing asymptotic dynamics at infection prevalence O(epsilon). The difficult feature is validating the entrance from an O(1) global initial seed on times diverging as epsilon^-2 in a fast-slow three-compartment system, not elementary inversion of a scalar normal form alone. This is a specific motivated mathematical classification, not a universal epidemiological forecast; no general theorem or noise extension is claimed.
residual_risks: Quantitative practical relevance for real epidemics is limited by deterministic fixed-population assumptions; no stochastic forecast or parameter estimation is furnished.

The crossover function is the canonical scalar cubic/quadratic normal-form integral, so value rests on concrete full-basin uniform realization and exact calibration, not a novel elementary transcendental function.

limitations: All epidemiological rates strictly positive, k1=lambda/N0, k2=k2*-epsilon/N0>0, epsilon>=0, strictly interior fixed-population simplex S+I+R=N0; initial state must be fixed as epsilon->0.
Fixed-epsilon t->infinity decay is pointwise in epsilon; singular crossover convergence is local uniform only for tau in compact subsets of (0,infinity).
No assertion for epsilon<0, I0=0, non-invariant total populations, stochastic models, time-varying parameters or epidemiological forecasting.
Existing source global attractivity and pitchfork are prior results; not credited as independently novel.
